knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Stopping, taking the hand out, keeping people away and calling the supervisor is the first action, because the sharp cannot be seen. Reaching in to look, or moving the bin, risks a puncture or spreads the contamination.
A rigid, labelled sharps container is the only option that keeps a sharp contained. General waste, cardboard boxes and washroom bins are not containers for sharps.
An untrained worker makes the area safe, keeps people away and reports. Mopping up, or covering and leaving a spill, are clean-up actions reserved to trained workers under SOP-23 or are unsafe.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied bin with a simulated sharp hidden under material, the candidate stops, keeps the hands out of the bin, and calls the supervisor. Pass condition: no hand enters the bin before the assessor confirms the supervisor has been called, observed by the assessor.

Given a supplied sharps container and a general waste bag, the candidate places a simulated sharp in the sharps container and confirms it is not in the general waste bag. Pass condition: no simulated sharp is placed in the general waste bag, observed by the assessor.

Given a supplied injury and near-miss form, the candidate records a simulated needle-stick near miss with the time, place, item, witnesses and first-aid steps. Pass condition: all five fields are completed and the form is passed to the supervisor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Completed simulated injury and near-miss form
Assessor note of the trained-worker status shown for the SOP-23 procedure
stopWorkCriteria: Candidate reaches into a bin or under furniture to find a sharp
Candidate places a sharp in general waste
Candidate handles a body fluid spill without the training for the SOP-23 procedure
Candidate works with an open cut and no waterproof dressing in place
Candidate does not report a simulated sharps contact
